 With the exception of a few injuries, and the assorted turnovers and penalties that leave coaches muttering, the season has gone pretty much as planned for Cambridge-South Dorchester High's football team."We had talked all season," first-year Vikings' head coach Rob Burnham said, "about doing the things we're supposed to do, and being successful, and work hard, and improve day after day. Get through the season undefeated. Get the number one overall seed in the (Class) 1A, and then we won't play the Sentinels until we go to Annapolis. Obviously, things changed on that."
Cambridge-SD did go undefeated during the regular season and earned the No. 1 overall seed when the state playoffs were reseeded last week.
As for meeting three-time defending 1A state champion Fort Hill in a potential state-title showdown in Annapolis? Well, that changed when the Sentinels forfeited five regular-season games for using an ineligible player. Fort Hill remained eligible for the postseason though, romped to a pair of regional victories, and come into Friday's 6:30 p.m. state quarterfinal at Cambridge-SD (10-0) as the No. 8 seed at 4-7.
"I met with our guys and said, 'Obviously the circumstances have changed and what we worked hard for isn't necessarily going to be given to us,'" Burnham said. "'We still have to go out and take it. So in order to get what we want we have to beat them. We just have to do it two weeks earlier than we had planned on.'"
A Cambridge-SD assistant last year, Burnham and Fort Hill head coach Zack Alkire agreed this is not the same Sentinels team that routed the Vikings, 38-20, in last year's state semifinals in Cumberland.
"We have a much better shot to run the ball on them this year than last year," Burnham said. "I've coached for 26 years and that was the best high school team I've seen regardless of classification in three different states. They were really good."
But that team that went on to win a third straight state title while extending its winning streak to 21 games, graduated 20 players, and is not as senior heavy this year.
"We play 10 sophomores throughout the course of a game and they've done really well for us," Alkire said. "There's been some growing pains. But the seniors have shown good leadership and gotten those guys to get us to where we are today."
One thing hasn't changed though with the Sentinels.
"Still the same ground-and-pound style of offense," Alkire said. "We try to spread you out when we can, but it's mostly going to be under center, ground and pound."
Leading that rushing attack is senior running back Jabril Daniels, who has toted the ball 156 times for 1,664 yards and 26 touchdowns this season. Braelyn Younger (43-485-9) is also a threat. And though senior quarterback Nash Cassell, who has completed 13 of 27 passes for 276 yards and six touchdowns, isn't a huge running threat, Alkire said he "does a great job of getting the ball where it needs to be."
That offense faces one of the Bayside Conference's quickest defenses.
"They're very aggressive defensively; try to cause problems in your backfield," Alkire said of Cambridge-SD.
But Burnham knows the unit he's called the backbone of his team since August, faces perhaps its biggest test of the season.
"Fort Hill football is Fort Hill football," Burnham said. "They play physical. They play fast. They do multiple things offensively. They run the ball consistently with multiple backs. We have to contain their run, limit their explosive plays on defense."
Cambridge-SD also possesses big-play talent, with senior quarterback Anthony Hughes and senior running back Sterling Perkins Jr., who has gained over a 1,000 yards this season.
"Offensively, we need to protect the football and then be opportunistic and make plays when we can," Burnham said.
Though the Sentinels have usually been at home during the past three postseasons, Alkire said his team has adapted to playing on the road after the ineligibility ruling.
"Just a matter of getting the kids in the mindset to be able to go on the road and endure some of the longer road trips, and experience some of the things that opposing teams have had to experience against us," Alkire said. "It's been a transition but the kids have accepted it and they moved on."
And though its date with Fort Hill has come two weeks earlier than expected, Burnham thinks the Vikings are ready.
"I think our kids are excited about an opportunity to prove ourself on a big stage against a quality opponent," Burnham said. "In order to get where we want to be we have to beat them.
